title: NovaQuill Studio — Account Brief (Customer Success)
body: Company: NovaQuill Studio (novaquill.ai) | Company ID (HubSpot): hq-000947-nq
Account owner (AE): Avery Cho | SE: Riley Patel | CSM: TBD (handoff pending if converts)
Current stage (as of 2026-03-21): technical evaluation / POC (moved forward from discovery)
Forecast close month: 2026-05 (was trending 2026-04; slipped due to security review + procurement cycle)
Estimated ARR range: 20k–50k (updated from earlier 5k–20k after expanded workload sizing)
Account tier: SMB (self-serve motion; prefers minimal AE involvement)
HQ region: North America | Employees: 51–200 | Industry: content automation
Primary initiative / why now:
- Ship a product-led RAG + summarization experience for their customers (support + website copy + internal doc search).
- Wants a forkable “one-click deploy” sample on Vercel showing Redwood Hosted API + streaming UI.
Key contacts (from calls/threads):
- Maya R. (CTO) — technical decision maker
- Sam (Eng Lead) — implementing POC and integration patterns
Intended Redwood product(s):
- Hosted API (primary).
- (New) Asking about rate limit controls + per-project keys in Console for internal teams; may influence expansion.
Use cases (confirmed):
- Doc search (RAG) across customer docs + internal knowledge
- Content summarization (token-heavy; very cost sensitive)
- Support-agent assistant
- Website copy generation
Data + architecture notes:
- Docs: primarily S3 + some markdown in GitHub repo.
- Volume: originally ~50k docs; updated estimate ~75k–90k docs at launch with steady weekly growth.
- Retrieval: experimenting with hybrid (BM25 + vector) in app layer; wants Redwood guidance on caching + batching in hosted mode.
- UI: Vercel (Next.js) with streaming chat UX; prefer Edge where possible but willing to use serverless Node runtime for auth token broker.
Latency + performance targets (updated):
- Earlier target: 150–400ms cold / 50–120ms warm.
- Updated POC target (what they’ll accept for v1): <350ms median retrieval step (warm) with caching, end-to-end streamed response perceived as “instant start” (first token <1.2s).
Model preferences / cost constraints:
- Prefers open/compatible models; exploring mid-sized quantized options to reduce cost.
- Strong focus on token efficiency for summarization workflows; wants recommended presets (quality vs cost).
Security + compliance requirements:
- Immediate: audit logging (who/what/when), retention controls, and clear guidance on key handling for Vercel deployments.
- SSO/SAML: originally “later”; updated ask: SSO is now required prior to production rollout (timing depends on their enterprise customer pilot).
- Key concern from engineering: API key exposure risk in Edge/client contexts.
What changed since the 2026-03-09 notes (important deltas):
- Example code delivered: internal quickstart repo for Vercel + Redwood Hosted API shared with Sam (includes serverless token exchange pattern).
- SDK direction: they are proceeding with Node for the Vercel reference app; Python remains for offline indexing scripts.
- CORS: no longer a top blocker after adopting server-side proxy + short-lived session token pattern.
- New blocker surfaced: need clarity on audit log export (API vs UI) for their internal security checklist.
Open blockers / risks (current):
- Security review: confirmation on audit log availability and retention configuration (UI + any export options).
- Procurement: they want an annual option if POC succeeds; need rough order-of-magnitude pricing guidance tied to projected query volume.
- Technical: needs recommended approach for prefix/KV caching and batching knobs in hosted mode (they are seeing cost spikes in summarization tests).
Competitors mentioned / alternatives evaluated:
- OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere (benchmarking quality/cost).
- Primary reason they’re still engaged: Redwood performance + desire for plug-and-play adapters and clearer deployment patterns.
POC plan (2-week spike → extended):
- Week 1: wire retriever (LangChain/LlamaIndex) → Redwood Hosted API → streaming chat UI on Vercel.
- Week 2: load test + latency measurement + cost profiling for summarization-heavy prompts.
- Extension (new): add audit log validation + SSO readiness check as gating for pilot.
Success metrics (still in play):
- Latency: <350ms median retrieval warm; first token <1.2s perceived start
- Quality: coherent, grounded summarization + citations/links back to source docs (nice-to-have but trending to requirement)
- Cost: target cost per 1k queries is still TBD by NovaQuill; they will decide after week-2 profiling
Customer success next steps (proposed):
- Provide a short “Security & Vercel Deployment Pattern” checklist (keys, token broker, CORS, recommended defaults).
- Confirm audit log capabilities + any export story (even if manual) and document retention options.
- If they hit POC metrics: prepare lightweight onboarding plan + recommend a CSM assignment for post-conversion (they want fast responses + self-serve docs).
Last activity:
- 2026-03-20: Sam confirmed quickstart repo deploy succeeded; asked follow-up questions on caching/batching and audit logs.
Internal notes (context + quotes):
- 2026-03-09 call: Maya + Sam very product-led; wants self-serve to work with minimal AE involvement.

- Quote (developer): “We like Redwood’s performance claims — just need plug-and-play adapters. If we can ship a Vercel sample that demos frontend chat calling a serverless proxy, we’ll try to convert during trial.”
Owner reminders (CS):
- Track whether SSO becomes a hard gate for contract signature.
- Watch for expansion potential if their customer-facing pilot succeeds (summarization volume could grow quickly).
